dict.string: PROSOCHE - Nine Circles (Dumb fork). This shortcut is the whole product: it reads two setup answers from import, checks for a saved setup file, creates one on first run along with a setup note, and opens that note. Later builds add the automation handling and the nine attention circles on top of this same file.

Shortcuts generated by Shortcuts Playground. May contain mistakes. Always check the shortcut's actions first.
This shortcut was created from the following build objective:
> A user can import the Shortcut, run it manually for the first time, and get a working state file plus a fully instructive Control Room note - and every subsequent invocation routes correctly and never corrupts or duplicates that foundation.
The next two actions are pinned in place: the import questions below are matched to their target actions by position in the list, not by name, so nothing may be inserted before them. A third import question, for on-device intelligence, belongs to a later build and is not part of this one.

--- CONFIGURATION: read the fixed tuning settings once, before routing ---
ALLOW_MANUAL_UNIT_CONVERSION: the settings text below includes the date pattern yyyy-MM-dd, which a broader safety check mistakes for a millimeter unit. There is no measurement or unit conversion anywhere in this shortcut.
--- CLOCK: build today's timestamp and day key once, before routing ---

--- STATE LOAD & BOOTSTRAP: reads or rebuilds the saved setup file once, above every routing path, so a manual tap, an automatic app-open, and an automatic app-close all reach it the same way ---
Guard against empty fields before reading anything nested inside them. Six fields in the setup file are empty on a freshly rebuilt document and stay that way until a later build fills them in: last_open_at, last_close_at, last_app, active_session, cooldown_until, and every key nested beneath active_session (its id, start time, app, intention, declared duration, and the rest). Reading a nested key while its parent is empty breaks instead of just coming back empty, so every later read of any of these six must first check that the field itself has a value. Nothing in this build reads any of them yet; a later build must follow this rule at the point where it starts to.

No action exists to check whether a file exists before reading it (this is a real gap in Shortcuts, recorded as DEV-02). This step tries to read the setup file directly with its own error dialog turned off, so a missing file falls through safely to the steps below instead of showing an error.

Build the two-field check that decides whether the saved setup counts as usable: its schema version must have a value, that version must match the one this build writes, and its profile must have a value too. Both values being compared were already read out through a Text action above and below, never compared as a raw dictionary value directly, because a direct comparison like that can wrongly come back blank. The version check compares text for an exact match rather than comparing numbers, since this app has no built-in way to check two numbers for equality.

Check the setup file's schema version first, as the outermost of three checks nested inside each other so all three must hold together for the setup to count as valid: - Input uses the schema version text read from the saved setup above. - If the schema version has no value at all, this saved setup is not valid; the checks below are skipped and the setup gets rebuilt. - If it has a value, continue to the version-number check nested below.

Check that the schema version is exactly the version this build writes: - Input uses the same schema version text checked above. - If the schema version is exactly 1, continue to the profile check nested below. - Otherwise this saved setup was written by a different version and does not count as valid; skip ahead and rebuild it.

Check that the setup file's profile field also has a value, the third and innermost of the three nested checks: - Input uses the profile text read from the saved setup and routed through a Text action above. - If the profile has a value, all three checks passed: mark the saved setup as valid below. - Otherwise this saved setup is missing its profile field and does not count as valid.

Decide whether to load the existing setup or rebuild it, using the single valid/not-valid result computed above: - Input uses the setup-is-valid result set above. - If it is exactly yes, the existing setup is valid; use it as already loaded above and write nothing. - Otherwise — whether the file is missing, unreadable, from an old version, or missing its profile field, all of which look identical from here — rebuild it fresh below.

Existing, valid setup was found and is already loaded above as the current setup. Nothing is written on this path, which is what keeps a later manual run, an automatic app-open, or an automatic app-close from ever overwriting a working setup.

No existing, valid setup was found — the file may be missing entirely, unreadable, from an old version, or missing its profile field; all four look identical from here and all get exactly the same safe rebuild. Create the setup folder first, ASCII-named so the file path never carries an accented character.

Turn the raw descent answer typed at import into one of exactly three known values, as two checks nested inside each other: - Input uses the descent answer captured at import. - If it is exactly Paradise, that becomes the setup's profile below. - Otherwise, check whether it is Inferno instead, nested below.

The import answer was not Paradise. Check whether it is Inferno instead: - Input uses the same descent answer checked above. - If it is exactly Inferno, that becomes the setup's profile below. - Otherwise — Limbo itself, a typo, or anything unrecognised — the setup's profile below always becomes Limbo, the documented default.

Turn the raw speaking-permission answer typed at import into a real yes/no value for the setup file, instead of storing the typed word as-is: - Input uses the speaking-permission answer captured at import. - If it is exactly yes, the setup file below stores a real true value. - Otherwise the setup file below stores a real false value, since a real true/false value reads back as a plain number later, never as the words true or false.

The starting setup file uses schema version 1 and stores the profile and speaking permission already turned into their normalised values above, not the raw text typed at import. Session history, contract history, and each exit's saved outcomes are capped so they never grow without bound: 20 sessions, 10 contracts, 20 outcomes per exit. The profile snapshot's synced time is recorded as plain text here; a later build turns it into a real number.

Saves directly to the setup folder's state.json path (folder and file name together), so the file always lands at the same fixed location on every run, matching the path used above to read it.

Record that this run had to rebuild the setup file, so a manual run can add one best-effort line about it to the setup note afterwards. Never gates or blocks anything: if a later manual run does not happen soon, this record is simply overwritten the next time a rebuild happens.
--- ROUTING: normalise the Shortcut Input into Input Key before any comparison ---

Route this run based on whether the normalised Input Key has a value, never the raw Shortcut Input: - Input Key is built just above by composing the Shortcut Input into text, trimming surrounding whitespace, then uppercasing the result. - Trimming an all-whitespace value leaves an empty string, and an empty string has no value, so a plain manual tap (no input at all) and a whitespace-only input both fall through to this gate's Otherwise below, the MANUAL branch, rather than being treated as unrecognised input. The very first run of a freshly imported Shortcut is exactly this case, since neither Personal Automation exists yet to send OPEN or CLOSE. - If Input Key has a value, this run came from an automation (or a stray caller) and is classified into OPEN, CLOSE, or an unrecognised fail-safe outcome below. - If Input Key is empty, this is a manual run and continues below to check for existing setup.

Compare the normalised Input Key to OPEN, the exact text Automation A's Run Shortcut step sends (per the Control Room Note's Automation A build steps): - Input uses the Input Key variable set above. - If Input Key is exactly OPEN, this run continues into the OPEN branch below. - Otherwise, this run continues below to check for CLOSE instead.

OPEN branch anchor. Phase 3 fills this with the OPEN pipeline (Heat, Gravity, Pressure, and the Circle they map to). The shared setup check that used to be described here now runs once, above this entire router, so every invocation mode already has a loaded, valid setup by the time execution reaches this point — Phase 3 does not need to repeat it. Nothing in this branch reads, writes, or changes anything in this plan.

Input Key was not OPEN. Compare it to CLOSE, the exact text Automation B's Run Shortcut step sends (per the Control Room Note's Automation B build steps): - Input uses the same Input Key variable tested above. - If Input Key is exactly CLOSE, this run continues into the CLOSE branch below. - Otherwise, this run continues below to the fail-safe branch, since Input Key is non-empty but neither OPEN nor CLOSE.
CLOSE branch anchor. Phase 4 fills this with the CLOSE pipeline (session measurement and the overrun/race protocol). Nothing in this branch reads, writes, or changes anything in this plan.

Input Key was neither OPEN nor CLOSE, and is not empty: unrecognised input, a mis-typed automation, or a stray caller (BOOT-02). This branch is inert by construction - it performs no file read, no file write, no dictionary mutation, no Note creation or append, and waits on nothing, because treating this as a real tracked-app open would inject a phantom event into Heat and Pressure, and a branch that waits on anything is a branch that can hang. It shows one diagnostic alert and ends.
PROSOCHĒ received input it did not recognise and took no action. Nothing was read, written, or changed.

# PROSOCHĒ — Control Room
## READ THIS FIRST
PROSOCHĒ notices when you open a chosen app. It measures how often and how automatically you have been reaching for that app, and the more automatic that reaching has become, the more it gets in your way before you arrive where you were actually going. It does not block anything. It does not decide anything on your behalf.
Two things about it should be plain from the start.
This Shortcut cannot create its own automations. Apple does not allow a shared shortcut to install a Personal Automation on your device. Automation A and Automation B below are something you build yourself, once, in the Shortcuts app. Nothing else in this Note will do that step for you.
PROSOCHĒ is bypassable. You can dismiss any interruption it shows you, at any time, without consequence. You can turn either automation off, or delete both, in the Shortcuts app whenever you want. It is not trying to stop you, and it does not claim otherwise.
### Automation A — OPEN
Build this in the Shortcuts app, with this Note open beside you.
1. Open the Shortcuts app. 2. Go to the Automation tab. 3. Tap the button to create a new Personal Automation. 4. Choose the App trigger. 5. Select the apps you want PROSOCHĒ to watch. 6. Choose Is Opened. 7. Turn off "Ask Before Running", so the automation runs immediately without asking. 8. Add the Run Shortcut action. 9. For the shortcut, choose the one named exactly PROSOCHĒ — Nine Circles — Dumb. 10. Set the Run Shortcut action's input to the text OPEN, typed exactly as those four capital letters and nothing else.
### Automation B — CLOSE
Build a second Personal Automation the same way as Automation A, with three differences: the same apps, the Is Closed trigger in place of Is Opened, and the input text CLOSE in place of OPEN.
1. Open the Shortcuts app. 2. Go to the Automation tab. 3. Tap the button to create a new Personal Automation. 4. Choose the App trigger. 5. Select the same apps you chose for Automation A. 6. Choose Is Closed, not Is Opened. 7. Turn off "Ask Before Running", so the automation runs immediately without asking. 8. Add the Run Shortcut action. 9. For the shortcut, choose the one named exactly PROSOCHĒ — Nine Circles — Dumb. 10. Set the Run Shortcut action's input to the text CLOSE, typed exactly as those five capital letters and nothing else, not OPEN.
Both automations are needed. Without CLOSE, PROSOCHĒ has no way to measure how long a session actually lasted, so it cannot tell whether a boundary you set for yourself was kept or exceeded.
## Do not target these apps
Do not point either automation at Phone, Messages, Maps, Wallet, an authenticator, a password manager, or any other app you might need in a hurry or in an emergency. PROSOCHĒ is meant for the apps you open without deciding to, not the ones you rely on.
## MY PHONE, ON PURPOSE
This section is yours. Write in it directly, here in the Notes app. Nothing here has to be tidy, and you can write naturally.
### What is my phone genuinely for?
Write a few things your phone does that improve your life. For example: communicate with the people I love; navigate; capture ideas; take photographs; make or listen to music; learn; organise my life; deliberately relax.
### Which apps take more attention than I intend to give them?
List the apps you are configuring the OPEN and CLOSE automations for. For example: Instagram, Facebook, Reddit, TikTok.
### What do I actually want the reclaimed attention for?
For example: books; making music; training; cooking; friends; my partner; my children; being outside; thinking; sleeping; doing nothing.
### When PROSOCHĒ stops an automatic open, what would I rather do?
Choose from the six exits PROSOCHĒ offers — Capture, Coordinate, Create, Connect, Consult, Close — and name the apps or actions you would actually prefer, for each one that fits you.
### What does deliberate leisure look like for me?
For example: ten minutes of Reels after dinner is fine; I do not want to turn five minutes into forty; I do not want to repeatedly check the same feed.
### Optional sentence to my future self
For example: I installed this because I was tired of checking without deciding.
PROSOCHĒ only reads this section when you explicitly ask it to, from the Control Room menu. It is not parsed on every app open.
## CURRENT SETTINGS
- Fork: Dumb - Profile: ￼ - Sequence: Classic - Voice: ￼ - AI: not used by this fork - Enabled exits: all six, by default — Capture, Coordinate, Create, Connect, Consult, Close
## CURRENT STATE
Nothing has been recorded yet. This is the first run. This section is rewritten each time PROSOCHĒ is run manually, so what you read here will change as you use it.
## ATTENTION LEDGER
Meaningful events are appended here as they happen: circle changes, boundaries set and then kept or exceeded, redirects, cool-downs, profile changes. Not every internal calculation is recorded here. Entries begin in later phases of this build.
## VALUE / LIFE RETURNED
Reserved. Nothing is measured here yet.
## SUPPORT PROSOCHĒ
Reserved. Nothing is asked for here yet.

Uses the camelCase content field, not the shorter one: the shorter spelling looks correct and passes checks here, but produces a note with no visible text once actually created. Since this note is the only place setup instructions are shown, that failure would be silent. No separate title field is documented for this note-creation action, so the note's name comes from its first line above, which is written to read exactly as the title a later build searches for.
Choose your descent: Paradise, Limbo, or Inferno. If you are not sure, choose Limbo.
May PROSOCHĒ speak to you at the highest circles? Answer yes or no.
